title: Pita Bread
description: Pita Bread is a traditional Arabic flatbread with a soft texture and signature pocket. Freshly baked, it is perfect for stuffing with fillings, serving alongside mezze, or dipping into hummus, baba ghanoush, and labneh.

instruction.title: Method
steps:
1. Activate Yeast:
• Mix warm water, sugar, and yeast.
• Let sit 5–10 minutes until frothy.

2. Make Dough:
• In a large bowl, combine flour and salt.
• Make a well in the center, pour in the yeast mixture and olive oil.
• Mix until a rough dough forms.

3. Knead:
• Knead on a lightly floured surface 8–10 minutes until smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky.
• Tip: Use the palm and push technique like professional bakers.

4. First Proof:
• Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth or cling film.
• Let rise 1–2 hours until doubled in size.

5. Shape Pitas:
• Punch down dough, divide into 80–90g pieces.
• Roll each into a ball, then roll into a 6–7 inch (15–18 cm) circle, 4–5 mm thick.
• Important: Even thickness ensures proper pocket formation.

6. Second Proof:
• Place circles on a lightly floured tray, cover with a cloth, and let rest 30 minutes.

7. Bake:
• Option A – Oven (Professional Style): Preheat oven to 250°C (480°F) with a baking stone or tray inside. Slide dough onto the hot stone/tray. Bake 3–5 minutes until puffed and lightly golden.
• Option B – Stovetop (Authentic Arabic): Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Cook each circle 1–2 minutes per side until puffed and golden spots appear.

8. Cool:
• Transfer to a clean cloth, cover, and let cool.
• Pitas will deflate slightly but retain a pocket.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve warm with hummus, baba ghanoush, or labneh.
Use for shawarma, falafel, or kebab wraps.
Pair with mezze platters and grilled meats.
Brush with olive oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds or za’atar before serving.

chefTips: High heat and a baking stone create instant steam, essential for puffing.
Don't over-flour the surface—too much flour prevents puffing.
Serve fresh; pita loses pocket structure over time.
